docs.title: NadekoBot Documentation
docs.text: NadekoBot is an open source Discord bot for moderation, games, XP and leveling, an economy with Nadeko Flowers, and hundreds of utility commands.

docs.title: Use the public bot
docs.text:
Add the public NadekoBot to your server. You do not install anything.

Add NadekoBot to your server Commands

docs.title: Host your own bot
docs.text:
Each option below needs your own Discord bot. First, create a Discord bot and copy its token. Then pick a guide:

Your setup Guide No server and no setup (paid hosting, free trial) NadeKloud Use a window app on Windows, Linux or macOS Desktop guide (Upeko) Use the terminal on Linux or macOS CLI guide Run the bot in a Docker container Docker guide Build the bot from its source code Source guide

A server keeps the bot online all day. Get a Linux server, then use the CLI guide or the Docker guide.

nadekloud Hosted NadekoBot

Want your own bot without the setup? NadeKloud is paid hosting for NadekoBot, with a free trial. It runs your bot for you, and you set it up in a web dashboard.

Try NadeKloud

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• AI agent: members ask the bot for things in plain language. To turn it on for your own bot, read Owner setup.
  • Waifu system: an economy game with waifus, fans and managers.
  • Medusa plugins: add your own commands to a self-hosted bot.

docs.title: Get help
docs.text:
• Ask in the NadekoBot Discord server.
  • Report a bug on GitHub. If you are not sure that it is a bug, ask in the Discord server first.
  • NadekoBot is open source. Donations keep the project alive.

docs.title: Creating your own Discord bot
docs.text: Before you install NadekoBot, you need a Discord bot account and its token. This page shows how to create the bot, get the token and invite the bot to your server.

docs.title: Create the bot and copy the token
docs.text:
1. Open the Discord Developer Portal and log in.
  2. Click New Application.
  3. Type a name for the bot.
  4. Accept the terms and click Create.
  5. On the left, click Bot.
  6. Click Reset Token, then click Yes, do it!.
  7. Copy the token.
  8. Put the token in the token field of creds.yml. Your install guide tells you where this file is.

Keep the token secret

The token is the password of your bot. A person with the token can control the bot. If someone sees your token, reset it immediately. A reset stops the old token, so put the new token in creds.yml.

docs.title: Turn on the privileged intents
docs.text:
1. On the Bot page, go to Privileged Gateway Intents.
  2. Turn on all three intents:
    • Presence Intent
    • Server Members Intent
    • Message Content Intent
  3. Click Save Changes.

Without these intents, some features do not work. Without Message Content Intent, the bot runs a command only when the message starts with a mention of the bot.

docs.title: Set yourself as the owner
docs.text:
The owner can use the owner-only commands, for example .die and .config. On the first start, the bot adds the owner of the Discord application to the ownerIds list. To add more owners, do these steps:

  1. In Discord, open User Settings > Advanced and turn on Developer Mode.
  2. Right-click your name and click Copy User ID.

  3. Put the ID in the ownerIds list of creds.yml:

    ownerIds:
  - 123456789012345678

docs.title: Invite the bot to your server
docs.text:
1. On the left, click General Information and copy the Application ID.

  2. In this link, replace YOUR_APPLICATION_ID with your Application ID:

    https://discord.com/oauth2/authorize?client_id=YOUR_APPLICATION_ID&scope=bot&permissions=66186303

  3. Open the link in your browser.

  4. Select your server and click Authorize.

The bot is now in your server. It stays offline until you start it.

docs.title: Next step
docs.text:
Install the bot with one of the guides:

  • Desktop guide (Upeko) for Windows, Linux and macOS
  • CLI guide for Linux and macOS
  • Docker guide
  • Source guide

docs.title: AI Agent Owner Setup
docs.text: This page is for the owner of a self-hosted NadekoBot. To use the agent on a bot which someone else hosts, read Usage and skills.

docs.title: Pick an AI provider
docs.text:
The agent needs an OpenAI-compatible chat API with tool calling (function calling). These providers work:

  • OpenAI
  • OpenRouter, which can send a request to other models if one fails
  • A local server (vLLM, llama.cpp) with an OpenAI-compatible API and a model with tool calling

A provider or model without tool calling refuses the requests of the agent, and the agent does not answer.

docs.title: Turn on the agent
docs.text:
1. Put your API key in aiApiKey in data/creds.yml, then restart the bot.

  2. Open data/ai-agent.yml and set these fields:

    enabled: true
# Without /v1/chat/completions at the end
apiUrl: https://openrouter.ai/api
modelName: openai/gpt-5.4

  3. Type .configreload aiagent in Discord, or restart the bot.

The bot needs the Message Content intent (see Create a Discord bot). Without it, only a mention of the bot starts the agent. The name trigger, the follow-up time and the channel memory then do not work.

You can also change most settings in Discord with .config aiagent <setting> <value>. For example: .config aiagent model openai/gpt-5.4. Type .config aiagent to see all settings.

Setting Default What it does enabled false Turns the agent on or off model gpt-5.4 The model name reasoning low The reasoning effort: none, low, medium, high or xhigh maxtools 10 The maximum number of tool calls in one request maxtokens 16384 The maximum number of tokens in one answer temperature 0.3 A lower value gives answers which change less memory 20 The number of recent channel messages which the agent remembers. 0 turns it off memoryexpiry 30 The minutes without activity before the agent forgets a channel useembed true false sends answers as plain text showactivity true Shows a live message with the steps of the agent

In data/ai-agent.yml, some of these settings have longer names, for example modelName, maxTokens, reasoningEffort and memoryIdleExpiryMinutes. To turn off reasoning, set reasoningEffort to an empty value in the file.

These settings are only in data/ai-agent.yml:

  • models: a list of models for providers like OpenRouter. When the first model fails, the provider tries the next one.
  • nameTriggerEnabled: the agent starts when a member says the name of the bot. Default true.
  • followUpWindowSeconds: the seconds after an answer in which a member can continue without a mention. Default 120. 0 turns it off.
  • allowedTools: the tools which the agent can use. Empty means all tools.
  • customHeaders: extra HTTP headers for each request to the provider.

docs.title: Choose who can use the agent
docs.text:
The bot owner can always use the agent. Other people can use it only when you allow them. The bot ignores everyone else.

Command What it does .agentwhitelist @user / .aiwl Allows one user, or removes the user again .agentwhitelistrole <role> / .aiwlr Allows all members of a role .agentwhitelistserver [server id] / .aiwls Allows all members of a server (default: this server) .agentwhitelistlist / .aiwll Shows who is allowed

If patronage is on (isEnabled: true in data/patron.yml), active patrons can also use the agent.

An alias, a scheduled command or a command which the agent runs never starts the agent.

docs.title: Edit the prompts
docs.text:
Two files in data/ai/prompts/ control how the agent talks. The bot creates them on the first start.

  • SOUL.md: who the bot is (name, personality, tone).
  • OPERATOR.md: your rules for the agent (topics, limits, things it must not do).

Every server sees the same two files. For rules of one server, use skills.

To edit a file in Discord, type .aiprompt, select SOUL or OPERATOR, then click Edit. You can also edit the files directly. The bot loads a changed file in about one second. A file can have up to 20 KB.

Warning

The Discord editor holds only 4,000 characters. If a file is longer, edit it on disk. When you save a longer file in the Discord editor, the bot keeps only the first 4,000 characters.

You can use these placeholders in the prompts:

  • {botName} and {botId}: the name and the ID of the bot.
  • {guildName}, {channelName} and {userName}: these work too, but they make the prompt different for each server, channel and user. Then the provider cannot cache the prompt, and each request costs more. The agent already gets these values in a separate message.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• The agent does not answer. Make sure that enabled is true, aiApiKey is set and the user is allowed. Look for errors from the provider in the bot's log.
  • The log shows AI embedding runtime (ONNX) failed to load. The agent is off until the next start. On Windows, install the Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable (x64).
  • The log shows unknown parameter: tools. The model does not support tool calling. Pick a different model.
  • A change in SOUL.md does not work. The log shows PromptLibrary: loaded SOUL after the bot loads the file. If you do not see it, save the file again or restart the bot.

docs.title: AI Agent Usage and Skills
docs.text:
The AI agent reads your request in plain language, runs the commands for it as you and replies with the result.

The bot owner turns on the AI agent and chooses who can use it. If the agent does not answer, ask the owner of the bot. The agent works only in a server channel, not in a direct message.

docs.title: Start the agent
docs.text:
Method Example Mention the bot at the start of your message @Nadeko what is my balance? Use the .agent / .ai command .agent show the top 5 xp members Reply to an answer of the agent, with the reply ping on and Bob? Say the name of the bot hey Nadeko, warn @Bob for spam

A mention and .agent start the agent for each request. A reply and the name of the bot start it only when your message looks like a request. "lol" or "thanks" does not start it.

After the agent answers, you can continue in the same channel without a mention. This works for 2 minutes (the bot owner can change this time). In this time, each message which you send in that channel goes to the agent:

@Nadeko how many flowers does Alice have?
  Alice has 5,000 flowers.
and Bob?
  Bob has 1,200 flowers.

To stop an answer which is running, type .agentcancel / .aic.

docs.title: Skills
docs.text:
A skill is an instruction which server admins add for the agent. A server skill works in all channels. A channel skill works only in its channel. A skill changes the style and the topics of the answers. It cannot give a member more permissions.

  • A server can have up to 10 skills. Server skills and channel skills count together.
  • A skill name can have up to 50 characters. An instruction can have up to 2,000 characters.
  • You need the Administrator permission.

docs.title: Server skills
docs.text:
A server skill works in all channels of the server.

Command What it does .agentskilladd <name> <instruction> / .aisa Adds a skill .agentskillremove <name> / .aisr Removes a skill .agentskilltoggle <name> / .aist Turns a skill on or off .agentskilllist / .aisl Shows the skills, with buttons to turn them on or off

Example:

.agentskilladd tone Reply in a calm, formal tone.
.agentskilladd prices Do not tell prices. Tell members to read #pricing.

docs.title: Channel skills
docs.text:
A channel skill works only in the channel where you add it. Use it for a channel with its own rules, for example a formal #support channel.

Command What it does .agentchannelskilladd <name> <instruction> / .aicsa Adds a skill to this channel .agentchannelskillremove <name> / .aicsr Removes a skill from this channel .agentchannelskilltoggle <name> / .aicst Turns a channel skill on or off .agentchannelskilllist / .aicsl Shows the skills of this channel

docs.title: Privacy
docs.text:
• The agent keeps the conversation only in memory, not in the database. It forgets the recent messages of a channel after 30 minutes without activity, and after a restart of the bot.
  • The agent reads your private data (for example your reminders) only for you. It cannot read the private data of another member.
  • The bot removes hidden tags and control characters from names and messages before the AI model sees them.

docs.text:

docs.title: NadekoBot CLI Guide (via Bash Installer)
docs.text: The bash installer downloads NadekoBot, adds your token, installs the music tools and starts the bot. Use it on a Linux server or on your own Linux or macOS computer.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
The installer works on these 64-bit systems:

  • Ubuntu 22.04, 24.04
  • Debian 12, 13
  • Linux Mint 21, 22
  • Fedora 42, 43
  • Rocky Linux, AlmaLinux 8, 9
  • openSUSE Leap 15.7, Tumbleweed
  • Arch Linux, Artix
  • macOS 14 (Sonoma) or later. Music does not work on macOS yet.

You also need:

  • Create a Discord bot and copy its token.
  • To keep the bot online all day, get a Linux server.

  • Install curl. Most systems already have it.

    Ubuntu, Debian, MintFedora, Rocky, AlmaopenSUSEArch, ArtixmacOS 
    sudo apt install curl

    sudo dnf install curl

    sudo zypper install curl

    sudo pacman -S curl

    Install Homebrew, then:

    brew install curl

docs.title: Install the bot
docs.text:
1. Go to your home folder, then download and start the installer:

    cd ~
curl -L -o n-install.sh https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nadeko-bot/bash-installer/refs/heads/v6/n-install.sh
bash n-install.sh

  2. Type 1 (Install) and press Enter.

  3. Type 1 to select the latest version and press Enter. The installer puts the bot in the nadeko folder.

  4. Press Enter to go back to the menu.

  5. Type 3 (Add Token), paste your token and press Enter. In most Linux terminals, paste with Ctrl+Shift+V.
  6. For music, type 4 (Install music dependencies) and press Enter. Type y at each question. The installer installs ffmpeg and yt-dlp. It also installs Deno if your system has no JavaScript runtime.
  7. Type 2 (Run) and press Enter. The bot comes online in your server.

The bot stops when you close the terminal. To keep it running, do the steps in the next section.

Your token, owner IDs and API keys are in nadeko/data/creds.yml. To edit the file, type nano nadeko/data/creds.yml. To save and exit nano, press Ctrl+X, then Y, then Enter. Restart the bot after you edit the file.

docs.title: Keep the bot running
docs.text:
tmux (Linux and macOS)systemd (Linux)

tmux keeps the bot running after you close the terminal.

  1. Stop the bot if it runs: press Ctrl+C.

  2. Start a tmux session:

    tmux new -s nadeko

  3. Type bash n-install.sh, then type 2 (Run).

  4. Press Ctrl+B, then D. The bot continues to run in the background.

To go back to the bot, type tmux a -t nadeko.

systemd starts the bot when the server starts and restarts it after a crash. The .die command stops the bot.

  1. Stop the bot if it runs: press Ctrl+C.

  2. In your home folder, create the service:

    cd ~
sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/nadeko.service > /dev/null <<EOF
[Unit]
Description=NadekoBot
After=network-online.target
Wants=network-online.target
StartLimitIntervalSec=120
StartLimitBurst=3

[Service]
User=$USER
WorkingDirectory=$PWD/nadeko
Environment=PATH=$HOME/.local/bin:$HOME/.deno/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin
ExecStartPre=-$HOME/.local/bin/yt-dlp -U
ExecStart=$PWD/nadeko/NadekoBot
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=10

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
EOF

  3. Start the bot now and at each boot:

    sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now nadeko
Task Command Stop the bot sudo systemctl stop nadeko Start the bot sudo systemctl start nadeko Show the bot's log journalctl -u nadeko -f

docs.title: Update the bot
docs.text:
1. Stop the bot. With systemd, type sudo systemctl stop nadeko. In other cases, type .die in Discord.

  2. Go to your home folder, then download and start the installer again:

    cd ~
curl -L -o n-install.sh https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nadeko-bot/bash-installer/refs/heads/v6/n-install.sh
bash n-install.sh

  3. Type 1 (Install), select the newest version, then type y.

  4. Start the bot again. With systemd, type sudo systemctl start nadeko. In other cases, type 2 (Run) in the installer.

The installer keeps your data folder. It also puts a copy of the old data folder in nadeko_backups.

docs.title: Config Guide (.config)
docs.text:
The bot keeps its settings in .yml files in the data folder, for example data/bot.yml and data/gambling.yml. You can change most settings in Discord with .config. Only the bot owner can use .config and .configreload.

These settings apply to the whole bot, not to one server. The database keeps the server settings.

docs.title: Change a setting in Discord
docs.text:
Command What it does .config Shows the list of configs. .config <config> Shows the settings of the config and their values. .config <config> <setting> Shows the value and the description of the setting. .config <config> <setting> <value> Sets the setting to the new value.

For example:

.config bot
.config bot color.ok
.config bot color.ok ff0000

.conf is a short form of .config. You can type only the start of the config name, for example .config gamb for gambling. Type enough letters to match only one config: ga matches both gambling and games. Type .h .config for help in Discord.

The bot saves the new value in the file at once. You do not have to restart the bot.

docs.title: Edit a config file
docs.text:
Some settings are only in the files, not in .config. To change them, edit the file:

  1. Open the file in the data folder with a text editor. The database page shows where the data folder is for each install. The table below shows the file of each config.
  2. Change the value and save the file.
  3. Type .configreload <config> in Discord, for example .configreload gambling. You can also restart the bot.

.creload, .confreload and .crel are short forms of .configreload.

Reload before you set a value with .config

Until you reload, the bot uses the old values. If you set a value with .config on that config before you reload, the bot writes all its old values to the file, and your edits are lost.

The files are YAML. Keep the indentation and the quotes as they are. If the file has a mistake, the reload fails, the bot keeps the old values and writes the error in its log. The bot does not start with a broken file. Make a copy of the file before you edit it.

A wrong setting name does not stop the reload. The bot ignores a name which it does not know, and the next .config change removes it from the file. Check the names with .config <config>.

Config File aiagent data/ai-agent.yml bot data/bot.yml fishing data/fish.yml gambling data/gambling.yml games data/games.yml images data/images.yml music data/music.yml patron data/patron.yml searches data/searches.yml utility data/utility.yml waifu data/waifu.yml xp data/xp.yml

.config shows the configs of your bot version. A new version can add configs.

docs.title: creds.yml
docs.text: data/creds.yml keeps the token, the owner IDs and the API keys. It is not a config of .config. After you edit it, type .credsreload or restart the bot. A new token needs a restart. With Docker, bot_token in the container settings replaces the token of creds.yml (see the Docker guide).

docs.title: Database Guide
docs.text:
NadekoBot keeps all server settings and member data in one SQLite file, NadekoBot.db. This page is for the owner of a self-hosted bot.

You do not have to make the file. The bot creates it on the first start.

docs.title: Find the database
docs.text:
The database is in the bot's data folder:

Install Database file Desktop guide (Upeko) data/NadekoBot.db in the folder of Install Path on the bot page. Click Data Folder in Shortcuts to open it. On Windows, the default folder is Documents\upeko\bot-xxxxx. CLI guide nadeko/data/NadekoBot.db in your home folder Docker guide data/NadekoBot.db in the bot's folder, for example ~/nadeko/data/NadekoBot.db Source guide nadekobot/src/NadekoBot/data/NadekoBot.db

The bot reads data in the folder where it starts. If you start the built program from bin/Release/net9.0 (for example from an IDE), the database is in bin/Release/net9.0/data. A build copies the files of src/NadekoBot/data into that folder and can replace the database there. Always start the bot from the same folder, and edit the database in that folder.

While the bot runs, you can also see the files NadekoBot.db-wal and NadekoBot.db-shm. They are part of the database. Keep them together with NadekoBot.db.

docs.title: Get a database tool
docs.text:
Windows and macOSLinux

Install DB Browser for SQLite.

Install the sqlite3 program:

sudo apt install sqlite3

On Fedora, use sudo dnf install sqlite. You can also use DB Browser for SQLite if your computer has a desktop.

docs.title: Edit the database
docs.text:
Stop the bot and make a backup first

If you change the file while the bot runs, you can lose the change or damage the file. A wrong change can break the bot. Always stop the bot and copy the files before you edit them.

  1. Stop the bot. Type .die in Discord, or click Stop Instance in Upeko. With systemd, type sudo systemctl stop nadeko. With Docker, type docker stop nadeko.
  2. Copy NadekoBot.db to a safe place. If NadekoBot.db-wal and NadekoBot.db-shm are in the folder, copy them too.

  3. Edit the database:

    DB Browser for SQLitesqlite3
    1. Click Open Database and select NadekoBot.db.
    2. Open the Browse Data tab.
    3. In the Table list, select the table.
    4. Click the cell which you want to change.
    5. Type the new value in the Edit Database Cell pane on the right.
    6. Click Apply.
    7. Click Write Changes.
    8. Close DB Browser for SQLite.

    1. Open the database. For example, with the CLI install:

      sqlite3 ~/nadeko/data/NadekoBot.db

      With Docker, the bot writes its files as root. Use sudo sqlite3 ~/nadeko/data/NadekoBot.db.

    2. Type .tables to show the tables, and .schema DiscordUser to show the columns of a table.

    3. Type your SQL. End each statement with ;. For example, to give a member 1000 currency:

      UPDATE DiscordUser SET CurrencyAmount = CurrencyAmount + 1000 WHERE UserId = 123456789012345678;

    4. Type .quit.

  4. Start the bot.

If the bot does not start after your change, restore the backup: stop the bot, move NadekoBot.db, NadekoBot.db-wal and NadekoBot.db-shm to a different folder, then copy your backup files back.

docs.title: Use SQL from Discord
docs.text:
The owner can also read and change the database in Discord, while the bot runs:

  • .sqlselect <sql> shows the result of a query which only reads. It works only in DMs with the bot.
  • .sqlselectcsv <sql> sends the result as a CSV file. It works only in DMs with the bot.
  • .sqlexec <sql> runs SQL which changes the database. The bot asks you to confirm first.

For example: .sqlselect SELECT UserId, CurrencyAmount FROM DiscordUser ORDER BY CurrencyAmount DESC LIMIT 10

Many changes have a command, for example .award for currency. Use the command when there is one.

docs.title: NadekoBot Desktop Guide (via Upeko)
docs.text: Upeko is a desktop app which installs, starts and updates NadekoBot. Use it on your own computer. The bot is online only while Upeko runs.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Create a Discord bot and copy its token.

  • Use one of these systems (64-bit):

  • Windows 10 or later

  • Ubuntu 22.04, 24.04
  • Debian 12, 13
  • Linux Mint 21, 22
  • Fedora 42, 43
  • Rocky Linux, AlmaLinux 8, 9
  • openSUSE Leap 15.7, Tumbleweed
  • Arch Linux, Artix
  • macOS 14 (Sonoma) or later. Music does not work on macOS yet.

docs.title: Install the bot
docs.text:
1. Download Upeko from the latest release:

    System File Windows upeko-win-x64.exe (upeko-win-arm64.exe on ARM) macOS upeko-osx-arm64.app.zip (Apple chip) or upeko-osx-x64.app.zip (Intel) Linux upeko-linux-x64 (upeko-linux-arm64 on ARM)

    On Linux, make the file executable before you start it: chmod +x upeko-linux-x64.

  2. Start Upeko and click Create Instance.

  3. For music, look at the three tools at the top: ffmpeg, yt-dlp and js (Deno). A red dot means that the tool is missing.

  4. Click the name of each missing tool to install it. The dot becomes green.

    Linux

    If the ffmpeg dot stays red, install ffmpeg with your package manager, for example sudo apt install ffmpeg. Then start Upeko again.

  5. Click the new bot to open its page.

  6. Click Download & Install. The download is about 90 MB. The installed bot needs about 490 MB of disk space.

  7. When the status is Ready, click creds.yml in Shortcuts. The file opens in your text editor. If no app opens, click Data Folder and open creds.yml with a text editor.

  8. Put your token between the quotes of the token field, then save the file.

docs.title: Start the bot
docs.text:
Click Start. The bot comes online in your server after a few seconds.

Data Folder in Shortcuts opens the bot's data folder, which has the database and the config files.

docs.title: Update the bot
docs.text:
1. If the bot runs, click Stop Instance.
  2. Click Check Updates on the bot page.
  3. If a new version is available, click Update. Upeko installs the new version and keeps your data folder.
  4. Click Start.

If the update fails, close each program that has a bot file open, then try again.

docs.title: Next step
docs.text: To keep the bot online all day, use the CLI guide or the Docker guide on a Linux server.

docs.title: NadekoBot Docker Guide
docs.text: The NadekoBot image is ghcr.io/nadeko-bot/nadekobot:v6. It has ffmpeg, yt-dlp and Deno, so music works without more steps. The bot keeps its database and config files in /app/data.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Create a Discord bot and copy its token.
  • Install Docker Engine with the Compose plugin.
  • To keep the bot online all day, get a Linux server.
  • The commands on this page are for Linux and macOS. On Windows, use Docker Desktop and type the commands in WSL.

docs.title: Start the bot
docs.text:
Docker Composedocker run

  1. Make a folder for the bot and go into it:

    mkdir -p ~/nadeko && cd ~/nadeko

  2. Create the file compose.yml (for example with nano compose.yml) with this text. Put your token in bot_token and your time zone in TZ:

    services:
  nadeko:
    image: ghcr.io/nadeko-bot/nadekobot:v6
    container_name: nadeko
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      TZ: Europe/Rome
      bot_token: YOUR_BOT_TOKEN
    volumes:
      - ./data:/app/data

  3. Start the bot and show its log:

    docker compose up -d
docker compose logs -f

  1. Make a folder for the bot and go into it:

    mkdir -p ~/nadeko && cd ~/nadeko

  2. Start the bot. Put your token in place of YOUR_BOT_TOKEN and your time zone in place of Europe/Rome:

    docker run -d --name nadeko --restart unless-stopped \
  -e TZ=Europe/Rome \
  -e bot_token=YOUR_BOT_TOKEN \
  -v "$PWD/data:/app/data" \
  ghcr.io/nadeko-bot/nadekobot:v6

  3. Show the log:

    docker logs -f nadeko

On the first start, the log shows lines like these. Then the bot comes online in your server.

[12:17:22 INF] | #0 | Pid: 1
[12:17:23 INF] | #0 | Database does not exist. Creating a new database...
[12:17:24 INF] | #0 | Shard 0 logging in ...
[12:17:25 INF] | #0 | All services loaded in 1.24s

To stop the log, press Ctrl+C. The bot continues to run.

If the log shows 401: Unauthorized, the token is wrong, and the container restarts again and again. Stop it with docker stop nadeko. Then put the correct token in compose.yml and type docker compose up -d. With docker run, type docker rm -f nadeko and run the command again with the correct token.

docs.title: Change the settings
docs.text:
The bot puts its files in the data folder: creds.yml, the config files and the database file NadekoBot.db. To change creds.yml, edit the file, then restart the bot:

nano data/creds.yml
docker restart nadeko

The bot writes these files as root. If your user is not root, use sudo nano data/creds.yml.

bot_token in the container settings replaces the token field of creds.yml. To change the token, change bot_token and start the container again as in step 2.

docs.title: Stop the bot
docs.text: The bot restarts after .die, because of restart: unless-stopped. To stop the bot, type docker stop nadeko.

docs.title: Update the bot
docs.text:
Docker Composedocker run 
cd ~/nadeko
docker compose pull
docker compose up -d

cd ~/nadeko
docker pull ghcr.io/nadeko-bot/nadekobot:v6
docker rm -f nadeko

Then start the bot with the same docker run command as before.

The update keeps the data folder.

docs.title: Linux Server Guide
docs.text: The bot stops when the computer that runs it stops. To keep the bot online all day, rent a small Linux server (a VPS). This page uses DigitalOcean. Other providers work the same way.

docs.title: Create the server
docs.text:
1. Create a DigitalOcean account with this referral link. You get free credit, and the NadekoBot project gets credit after you spend $25.
  2. Click Create > Droplets.

  3. Select these options:

    Option Value Region The region nearest to you Image Ubuntu 24.04 (LTS) x64 Droplet type Basic CPU options Regular Size $6 per month (1 GiB memory, 1 vCPU, 25 GiB disk) Authentication Method Password. Select SSH Key only if you already added a key to DigitalOcean.

  4. Click Create Droplet.

  5. On the Droplets page, copy the IP address of the new droplet.

docs.title: Connect to the server
docs.text:
On Windows 10 or 11, open PowerShell. It has SSH, so you do not need PuTTY. On Linux or macOS, open Terminal. Then type this command with your IP address:

ssh root@YOUR_SERVER_IP

The first time, type yes to trust the server. If you selected a password, type it. The terminal does not show the password while you type.

When you see root@...:~#, you are on the server. Install the updates:

apt update && apt upgrade -y

If a window asks which services to restart, press Enter.

docs.title: Next step
docs.text: Install the bot with the CLI guide or the Docker guide.

docs.title: Setting Up NadekoBot from Source
docs.text: Build NadekoBot from its source code. Use this guide if you want to change the code. For a normal install, use the desktop guide, the CLI guide or the Docker guide.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Create a Discord bot and copy its token.
  • Install the .NET 9 SDK.
  • Install Git.
  • Install a text editor, for example Visual Studio Code.

docs.title: Install the bot
docs.text:
Open a terminal: PowerShell on Windows, Terminal on Linux and macOS. The commands are the same on all three systems.

  1. Go to the folder for the bot, for example your home folder:

    cd ~

  2. Download the source code and go to the bot project:

    git clone https://github.com/nadeko-bot/nadekobot -b v6 --depth 1
cd nadekobot/src/NadekoBot

  3. Make the credentials file:

    cp data/creds_example.yml data/creds.yml

  4. Open data/creds.yml in your text editor. Put your token between the quotes of the token field, then save the file.

  5. Build and start the bot:

    dotnet run -c Release

The bot comes online in your server. It uses the files in src/NadekoBot/data.

docs.title: Install the music tools
docs.text:
For music, the bot needs ffmpeg, yt-dlp and Deno in your PATH.

WindowsLinuxmacOS 
winget install Gyan.FFmpeg
winget install yt-dlp.yt-dlp
winget install DenoLand.Deno

Then close PowerShell and open it again. If music does not play, install the latest Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable (x64).

sudo apt update
sudo apt install ffmpeg curl unzip
mkdir -p ~/.local/bin
curl -L -o ~/.local/bin/yt-dlp https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/releases/latest/download/yt-dlp_linux
chmod +x ~/.local/bin/yt-dlp
curl -fsSL https://deno.land/install.sh | sh

On Fedora, use sudo dnf install ffmpeg-free unzip. On other systems, install ffmpeg with your package manager. Make sure that ~/.local/bin is in your PATH.

The voice files in data/lib are for x64 only. On an ARM computer, music does not work.

brew install ffmpeg yt-dlp deno

Music does not work on macOS yet, because the bot has no macOS voice files in data/lib.

docs.title: Update the bot
docs.text:
1. Stop the bot: press Ctrl+C, or type .die in Discord.

  2. Make a copy of the data folder:

    cd ~/nadekobot/src/NadekoBot
cp -r data ~/nadeko-data-backup

    If ~/nadeko-data-backup exists, delete it first.

  3. Download the new code:

    git pull --autostash

  4. Start the bot:

    dotnet run -c Release

--autostash keeps the changes which the bot made in its config files. If Git shows refusing to merge unrelated histories, clone the bot again and copy your data folder from ~/nadeko-data-backup into src/NadekoBot/data. If Git shows a different conflict, ask in the NadekoBot Discord server.

docs.title: Creating a Medusa
docs.text: This page shows how to make, build and load a medusa. The project template has example commands. You can see the template on GitHub.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Install the .NET 9 SDK.
  • Use a NadekoBot which you host yourself, version 7 or later.
  • Optional: install a code editor, for example Visual Studio Code.

docs.title: Make the project
docs.text:
1. Open a terminal and go to the folder for your projects.

  2. Make a folder for the medusa and go into it:

    mkdir example_medusa
cd example_medusa

  3. Install the template from the NadekoBot MyGet feed:

    dotnet new install nadeko-medusa --nuget-source https://www.myget.org/F/nadeko/api/v3/index.json

  4. Make the project:

    dotnet new nadeko-medusa

The project uses the newest Nadeko.Medusa 7 package. To use the package version of your bot, open example_medusa.csproj and change 7.* to your bot version, for example 7.8.0.

docs.title: Build and load the medusa
docs.text:
1. Build the medusa:

    dotnet publish -o bin/medusae/example_medusa

  2. Copy the folder bin/medusae/example_medusa into the data/medusae folder of your bot. The folder and the .dll file must have the same name: data/medusae/example_medusa/example_medusa.dll.

  3. In Discord, type .meload example_medusa.
  4. Try the example commands:
    • .hello
    • .hello @someone
    • .info John,24
  5. Type .meinfo example_medusa to see its sneks and its number of commands.
  6. Type .meunload example_medusa to unload it.

docs.title: Parts of a medusa
docs.text:
Part What it is Medusa The project. It builds into one .dll file, with optional extra files. It can have sneks, param parsers and services. Snek A class which becomes one module of the bot. Each snek has one instance while the medusa is loaded. Snek command A method with the [cmd] attribute. It works like a normal bot command. Param parser A class which turns the text of an argument into your own type. Service A class with the [svc] attribute, which you can inject into sneks and commands.

The base classes are open source in Nadeko.Medusa.

docs.title: Snek
docs.text:
• A snek can have one level of sub-sneks. A sub-snek is a nested class in the snek class. It cannot have more sneks in it.
  • A snek can have a prefix. If the prefix is test, the command cmd becomes .test cmd.

docs.title: Snek command
docs.text:
• The first parameter is the context. It sets where the command works:
    • AnyContext: in servers and in direct messages
    • GuildContext: only in servers
    • DmContext: only in direct messages
  • Parameters with the [inject] attribute come after the context and before the normal parameters. The bot puts services in them.
  • Commands support default values, [leftover] and params.
  • [user_perm] and [bot_perm] set the permissions which a command needs. [bot_owner_only] makes a command owner-only.
  • A command can return ValueTask, Task, Task<T> or void. The bot does not load a command which returns ValueTask<T>.

docs.title: Param parser
docs.text: A param parser inherits from ParamParser<T>. The template has EmployeeInfoParser, which turns John,24 into an EmployeeInfo. The bot keeps its own parsers. If your parser is for a type which the bot already parses (for example IGuildUser), the bot ignores your parser. Use your own types.

docs.title: Service
docs.text: Most medusae do not need services. Mark a class with [svc(Lifetime.Singleton)] or [svc(Lifetime.Transient)], then inject it with [inject].

docs.title: Strings
docs.text:
Keep the response strings and the command descriptions in one of three places:

  • res.yml and cmds.yml in the project folder. Use this if you do not need translations now. The build copies the files to the output.
  • The strings folder, for translations: strings/res/en-us.yml and strings/cmds/en-us.yml, and one more file in each folder for each language, for example strings/res/ru-ru.yml.
  • In the code. Put the command description in the [cmd] attribute, and send text which is not translated.

If res.yml exists, the bot ignores the strings/res folder. If cmds.yml exists, the bot ignores the strings/cmds folder. The template has both files, so delete them when you change to the strings folder.

When you change a response file of a loaded medusa, type .stringsreload. The bot loads the new strings without a reload of the medusa.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
A snek can override these methods:

Method When the bot calls it InitializeAsync When the bot loads the medusa. DisposeAsync When the bot unloads the medusa. ExecOnMessageAsync First, for each message. Return true to stop the bot from processing the message. ExecInputTransformAsync Next. Return the new text of the message, or null to keep it. The bot looks for a command in the new text. ExecPreCommandAsync After the bot finds a command (of any module), before it runs. Return true to stop the command. ExecPostCommandAsync After a command runs without an error. ExecOnNoCommandAsync When no command runs: the bot finds no command, or a check stops the command. The bot calls this method or ExecPostCommandAsync, never both.

docs.title: Unload problems
docs.text:
The bot can unload a medusa only when nothing holds a reference to its code. To keep your medusa unloadable:

  • In DisposeAsync, remove each reference which the bot or its services have to your objects (for example event handlers).
  • Keep commands short. A long task holds a reference to your code.

If a medusa does not unload, type .meunload, then restart the bot. To find the cause, read the .NET guide to assembly unloadability.

If a medusa breaks the bot and you cannot unload it, remove its name from the loaded list in data/medusae/medusa.yml, then restart the bot.

docs.title: Getting Started with Medusa
docs.text:
A medusa is a plugin for a self-hosted NadekoBot. It adds commands and features without a change to the bot's code. You can load, unload and update a medusa while the bot runs.

A bot on NadeKloud cannot load medusae.

docs.title: Manage medusae
docs.text:
Put each medusa in its own folder in data/medusae. The folder and the .dll file must have the same name, for example data/medusae/mymedusa/mymedusa.dll. Then use these owner-only commands:

Command What it does .medusalist / .melist Shows the folders in data/medusae, and which of them are loaded .medusaload <name> / .meload Loads a medusa .medusaunload <name> / .meunload Unloads a medusa .medusareload <name> / .mereload Unloads a medusa and loads it again .medusainfo <name> / .meinfo Shows the description, the sneks and the number of commands of a medusa

The bot loads the same medusae again after a restart. It keeps the list in the loaded list of data/medusae/medusa.yml.

docs.title: Use only medusae which you trust
docs.text:
Danger

A medusa runs with all the rights of the bot. A bad medusa can steal your bot token, and it can read and delete the files on the computer.

  • Load only medusae which you wrote, or which come from a person you trust completely.
  • Run the bot on a server which runs nothing else.

To find medusae from other people, ask in the #dev-and-modding channel of the NadekoBot Discord server.

docs.title: Make a medusa
docs.text: You write a medusa in C#. You need some knowledge of C# and .NET. Read Create a medusa.
